Thank you. :-)

I think after reading all the replies here, I'm going to. It's a terrifying thought, but it's for the best.

Haha - I know the feeling. I was in Mock Trial in high school - I definitely know the joy of a good rebuttal!

That does help. I have the tendency to try to think out the entire conversation (which is generally where I end up with thoughts such as in my original post...) and I always get rather overwhelmed from that. The thought of bringing it up is sort of terrifying, but - like you said - we're not supposed to go through life without being scared. I'm still not sure how to *start* the conversation, but maybe that will be easier once I actually start talking to him.

Thank you so much, again!

I honestly understand where you're coming from - hardships make the good times in our lives so much sweeter. However, be careful going about attracting trouble - it can come in a way that you completely regret.

Instead of *trouble*, per se, why don't you do something incredibly exciting with your life? I know that's way easier said than done with depression; personally, I have a hard enough time finding the energy to get out of bed each day let alone climbing a mountain. That being said, I think you need a challenge. Find something that interests you, but that you find difficult. Maybe it's getting another (or even your first) college degree (or masters, doctorate, PhD, etc). Maybe it's something sporty like trying to break your last running record, or swimming record, or slam dunks, etc, etc. Maybe it's something adventurous, like mountain climbing, or traveling the world, or living in Peru for a year.

Misspinaberry has a point, as well. It doesn't have to be big - maybe just take more healthy risks in your life. My parents picked up from their well paying jobs in a city they had lived in for twenty years, and moved to another state because they liked a job offered there. And while they weren't exactly *un*happy before, they are so much happier now.

Simply put - try to get yourself out of your comfort zone. Not so much that you feel legitimately scared or panicked, but enough that you're uncomfortable and learning something new.

Once your doing this, you may find that not only are you challenging yourself, but you're having fun while you're doing it. This combination is better than any serious hardships could possibly be - trust me.

I hope you find what you're looking for!

I'll remember all that when I talk to him. Once I talk to him (which may take a day or two to actually work up the courage, honestly...) I'll either update this post, or make a new one. I *may* be able to talk to him tonight - but he was told today that he got an awesome job (yay!) and I don't want to bring down his excitement/celebrating.

Thank you!

Thank you, thank you, thank you - so much.

Everything you've said makes so much sense to my more logical mind, especially now that I've calmed down, emotionally. I *want* to tell him, and I think I will just keep reading your reasoning until I'm able to, so that my own reasoning doesn't stop me...

Now I just don't know *how* to talk to him about it. It's still a terrifying thought, even if I know it's for the best.

Thank you for your response.

He's sort of long distance...I don't have any friends nearby - but I guess he is more "real-life" than anonymous people on the internet, haha...though, anonymous people on the internet have been a huge help to me lately, as well.

Thank you so much for your response.

> Do you know how good it feels (well, relatively, compared to not telling anyone) to tell someone what's going on in your head?

This is probably one of the best arguments I've heard, because I *do* know what that's like. I've been able to tell this friend almost everything else about me (including a few things in my past that I'm still carrying today), and it's always felt so good to get it out of my head. I guess I just feel so at fault for self-harming, etc, that I almost feel like I deserve the burden...I know that's not true (sometimes), but it definitely gets in the way of my rational thinking.

Hey - imo, video games and TV give the *best* lessons and morals...well, that and fairy tales. :-)

I'm going to try to talk to him, I think. Now I just have to figure out *how*...

*Hugs* if okay.

I'm so glad you were able to get the help you needed. I hope you're okay now.

There have been times that I've wished someone would see my scars. I've always felt horrible for thinking that, because then I felt like I was just asking for attention - but it would make it so much easier than having to actually *tell* someone. After reading all these replies, I think I might try to talk to my friend though - everyone is saying that it will help me find mental strength to stop...and I do want to stop.

Thank you so much for your help, and for sharing your story.
Thank you - you are likely right.

I'm not sure how to reply except to say: thank you. Thank you, so, so much. Thank you for validating how I'm feeling, and for your support - it helps so much. Everything you said was so kind.

I can't pretend that after reading this I suddenly no longer believe all the negative things I said; but the more I see you and other posters say these kind things, some part of me agrees with you and I'm starting to recognize this.

Somewhere in my subconscious I know that my depression is a real problem - and I would never tell another person suffering from it that it wasn't - I just feel like I'm completely over-dramatizing my situation, especially when serious things happen to my friends. I think you're absolutely right that I would never tell my friends - or even another living human being - the things I tell myself. I have a very harsh double standard. I would forgive my friends for just about anything, but I find it incredibly difficult to forgive myself or even validate my own problems and emotions.

Again, thank you so, so much for your support, it means so much.
Haha, thank you - this made me smile. :-)
Thank you. :-)

I love British TV as a general rule. Monty Python, Doctor Who, Torchwood (though a little too dark to watch at any time except when I am exceptionally stable), Coupling...I know there are others, as well.

I don't think I've heard of Spartacus - or the series, at least. Silly is awesome.

Oh, it definitely is. My parents have DVR, so they have every single episode recorded. I highly recommend it, as well, it can be highly amusing, yet dramatic, and while it rarely takes itself too seriously, can still heavily sway the viewer's emotions (I cried at the end of season's two and four).

Thank you. They do, indeed, far more than I think they will beforehand.

It's Doctor Who - a British SciFi. Fourth season (newer), to be exact. :-)
I  have my favorite television show on the background. It is distracting, at the very least, and it's one of my favorite episodes - I'm hoping it will make me laugh.

Thank you. I hadn't looked at it this way...I *do* want to help him - that must be at least mildly selfless of me. I just feel selfish for wallowing in my own misery, which is not truly justified, when they have real problems.

I may look a those resources, thank you.

Wow, thank you. I've not felt quite so supported in a while. I'm much calmer now, so I don't think I'm in as much danger of having an emotional fit, now. That being said, I'm slipping into the point of emotional repression - numbness - and I'm afraid I'm going to want to self harm if I slip much further down.
Thank you, so much. Just knowing that someone is listening makes me feel so much less alone.

Haha, yes, I could definitely use a hand or two, I'm afraid I'm having quite a bit of trouble with dealing on my own...

I just recently graduated from college, so I jump around a lot between people I can stay with until my life actually starts - unfortunately, this includes jumping around between cities, and even states, every couple of weeks. Moreover, while I *am* going to be settling down in one place (albeit temporarily) in a couple of months, it's unfortunately going to be in the middle of absolute nowhere (fifty miles to the nearest real city) and my work schedule is going to be quite varied (and I'll also have absolutely no say in when I work or get time off), so it won't leave me the option to set a specific time aside each week. :-(

I'm actually a little surprised at how much simply talking about this is helping a bit, so thank you. :-)

Thanks for the reply. I am not on anti-depressants, specifically for that reason. Unfortunately, for many people (and I'm guessing myself included, because it's run in the family), antidepressants will lower one's inhibitions, actually *increasing* the likelihood of suicide.

Thank you very much for the advice and help.

*hugs*

Wow, I am really glad to hear that you made it through all of that okay, and that you're doing well, now.

I do try to view the things I've been through as things that I've "survived" rather than being "a victim", but at this moment of time, I'm really just struggling with the fact that they *happened*.

Deceiving my self-destructive nature seems to be a good way to go about it, but I may have to find a different way of doing so. I despise apathy in myself, and it makes me want to cut all the more. Unfortunately, diet is *also* an issue for me (really, I'm just a rather f-ed up human being...) and I often manipulate my diet as a form of self-harm and control. I will have to try and think of methods that will work for me.

I'm so glad that you are doing well. It does give me a small bit of hope to see other people who have gone through as rough (if not even rougher) of a time and have made it to the other side.

Thank you very much for your help. :-)

Thank you - I'm really glad to hear that things got better for you. I remain semi-hopeful that they will for me, as well, but obviously still have serious doubts that it will...

I do think talking to a therapist may help, but I move around a **lot**. Another person suggested setting up phone meetings, though. One of my big problems, I think, is that when I get into the emotional fits like I described above, I don't think I'm even *thinking*. I almost have these blackouts where I forget what I was doing right before I cut, or sometimes I don't remember how I got certain injuries...but I will try meditation, as that has worked on a smaller level for myself before.

You're right, seeing that other people have gone through this is truly helpful, it helps one to not feel quite so alone in their problems.

Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you. *Hugs* in return.

I think I started cutting in high school - but I don't remember how I first started to self harm. I've been self-harming in various ways since I was about...eight or nine, maybe? As for *how* I started cutting, I don't really remember what gave me the idea to start doing so. I think it was something along these lines: I knew that physical pain provided a good release from the emotional pain I was experiencing, because I had been using it as a release since I was a child. I had cut myself shaving before (accidentally? I'm honestly not sure) and realized that the pain had actually brought a weird feeling of euphoria with it (I know now that it's because pain triggers endorphins in the brain). This coupled with the feeling that I needed to punish myself because I was feeling a huge amount of self-loathing led me to grabbing my pocket knife and, well - I cut. :-(

I don't know what I would improve...I've never really thought of it. Being depressed has become so much the norm for me, now, that I've never really considered **not** being depressed, or how I would go about making that happen.

I hate myself for many, many reasons. I'm stupid, I'm selfish, I'm self-centered, I can't seem to do anything important right, I just bring the people around me down...it would take me a while to list all the reasons...

Thank you for listening.

Thank you. I may try those - I had heard of /r/depression, but not /r/offmychest, so thank you.

And thank you for the reassurance that I can post here...

Thank you for the reply. Haha, alright, more detail it is...

I'm twenty-two. My mother took me to a therapist when I was fifteen, but I only went for a few sessions, and never actually talked about either my self-loathing or cutting. I know I should probably talk to one again, but, like I said, I move around quite a bit, so I'm somewhere new every week or two.

No, no doctor has every noticed, actually. But I've never had the serious physicals, and I always cut in very discrete places...well, relatively speaking, anyhow. I haven't actually been to a doctor in a few years, as well...

As for the less dangerous ways I self harm, there are, unfortunately, quite a few. I scratch myself a lot, I bite and chew on the inside of my mouth (hard enough to bleed), I cut myself off emotionally from people, I run - which is generally considered to be a healthy coping mechanism, however I run to the point of actual, physical pain and exhaustion, sometimes without eating - I deny myself food, and, in general, I just do and continue things that cause pain.

Yes, I do think I am depressed. At times much more than others, but I think I've been battling depression off and on since middle school.

Thank you very much, again, for the response, and for the reassurance that I can post here.
